subject: Commitment playbook: technical eval -> legal sequencing and target close
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Amanda Park <amanda.park@vitalityhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Commitment playbook: technical eval -> legal sequencing and target close

Amanda —

Great to meet earlier this week. We put together a short commitment playbook so both teams are aligned on the evaluation milestones and contractual sequencing. High-level asks from your side: a week-by-week evaluation cadence, procurement contact, and any mandatory security artifacts.

Proposed next steps:
- We’ll share a first-draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that maps milestones to owners (tech, legal, procurement).
- Confirm procurement contact + preferred contract flow (MSA first vs. order form first).
- Share SOC2/pen-test artifacts and security questionnaire for your review.

Target close: early June if we get procurement aligned in the next two weeks. Is that realistic for Vitality?

Attaching: Redwood_MAP_v1.pdf (draft MAP — milestones + dependencies).

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0187
Redwood Inference — production-first LLM inference

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_v1.pdf
From: Amanda Park <amanda.park@vitalityhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@vitalityhealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 May 2025 11:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Commitment playbook: technical eval -> legal sequencing and target close

Ben —

Thanks for the MAP. Quick answers: procurement here is procurement@vitalityhealth.com (cc’d). We can move fast on the evaluation — engineering can start a two-week pilot as soon as we have a clear scope.

Contract preference: procurement typically wants a signed MSA (legal baseline) before a formal order form/PO. That said, we’ve done parallel flows where commercial terms are finalized in the order form while MSA redlines run in parallel. Key ask from my side: we need a DPA (data handling) and your SOC2 report before committing to a PO.

Proposed timeline (tentative):
- 5/12: Share procurement contact and SOC2 request (done).
- 5/13–5/20: Tech pilot (2 weeks).
- 5/21–5/28: Finalize commercial order form and internal approvals.
- Target close: by 6/5 if no major legal blockers.

Also attach: Vitality_Security_Questionnaire_v2.xlsx — helps our security team triage.

Best,
Amanda Park
Director, Clinical Integrations | Vitality Health
amanda.park@vitalityhealth.com

Attachments: Vitality_Security_Questionnaire_v2.xlsx
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Amanda Park <amanda.park@vitalityhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 May 2025 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commitment playbook: technical eval -> legal sequencing and target close

Amanda —

Appreciate the clarity. We’ll proceed with the two-week pilot and aim to close by 6/5. To accelerate legal we recommend the following sequencing in the MAP (flexible):

Option A (preferred by commercial):
- Execute a lightweight order form + PO that captures pricing and pilot scope (fast).
- Run MSA/DPA redlines in parallel; require countersigned MSA/DPA before production ramp.

Option B (procurement-preferred):
- Sign MSA/DPA first (legal baseline), then finalize order form/PO.

We’ve attached a one-page MAP that maps these options and dependencies. Our legal lead (Karthik) is cc’d — he’ll review the DPA expectations.

Milestone ask for Vitality: please confirm the internal approver for contract signatures and any deadlines for fiscal Q2 purchasing.

Thanks,
Ben

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_v1.pdf (updated link)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Vitality sequencing + redline prep (please review)

Karthik / Laura —

Amanda confirmed procurement@vitalityhealth.com as the PO owner and flagged a preference for MSA first, but is open to parallel flows. They require SOC2 + our DPA before signing. Attached is a nominal redline we can push as a starting point. Quick thoughts:

- Karthik: can we prepare a DPA appendix that’s narrowly scoped to the pilot data types (de-identified clinical metadata + embeddings)? If we constrain scope we should reduce back-and-forth.
- Laura: commercial needs a one-page order form ASAP to secure the pilot PO — can you draft pricing + pilot scope (2 weeks, up to 25k tokens/day) and share by EOD?

I’ll coordinate with Amanda to lock the target close of 6/5 and confirm their internal approver.

Thanks — Ben

Attachments: redline_msa.docx
From: Amanda Park <amanda.park@vitalityhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@vitalityhealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 May 2025 13:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Commitment playbook: technical eval -> legal sequencing and target close

Ben —

Procurement confirms they can review a one-page order form immediately; PO issuance contingent on SOC2 + DPA. Our target for internal sign-off is 6/2 to allow legal a week for redlines; if we hit that checkpoint, 6/5 close is realistic.

Security team notes: they expect the DPA to include subprocessor visibility and a deletion/retention schedule. We’ll use the attached questionnaire to map gaps — can your security or legal team complete the items marked "Redwood action" and return by 5/20?

Also confirm: who will be the signatory on the Vitality side? I’ll loop our GC once procurement has the MSA draft.

Best,
Amanda

Subject: Re: Commitment playbook: technical eval -> legal sequencing and target close

Amanda —

Thanks — we’ll turn around the security items marked Redwood action and send a redline DPA by 5/19. Laura will drop a one-page order form with pilot pricing by EOD tomorrow (5/16).

Summary / mutual action plan (short):
- 5/16: Redwood sends one-page order form (Laura) + drafting DPA redline (Karthik).
- 5/20: Redwood returns completed security questionnaire sections and updated DPA.
- 5/21–5/28: Vitality final internal approval / PO issuance window.
- 6/2: Target MSA/DPA finalization (Vitality GC review).
- 6/5: Target production enablement / commercial close.

Risks: extended DPA negotiations or new subprocessor requests could push sign-off beyond 6/5. If procurement needs earlier PO for internal runway, we can provide a short-term engagement letter for pilot billing while legal completes the MSA.

I’ll follow up with a single-sheet MAP that encodes the milestones above and owners.

Best regards,
Ben Carter
